evidence: Plaut. Capt. 3.5.1: manicās alicui injicere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also the long sleeves of a tunic (see sleeve). To handcuff someone, manicās alicui injicere.

phrases.source: Traupman 195; Plaut. Capt. 3.5.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. manicae)

phrases.latin: Vigilēs meī apprehendērunt istōs grassātōrēs et manicās eīs injēcērunt.
phrases.english: My officers arrested those hoodlums and put handcuffs on them.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 195, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 325.
